CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region of Paser Regency.

Regent is the Regent of Paser Women are all women who are both inside and outside the household Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.

Physical violence is an act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Household neglect is any person who neglects another person in their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party given at the stage of investigation, inquiry, determination and upon examination in court hearings.

Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.

Service is an action that must be immediately taken to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim (woman) will, is or has occurred.

Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.

Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children.

Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house Gender is a characteristic inherent to men and women that is socially and culturally constructed.

Gender injustice is a system and structure in which both men and women become victims of that system.

Gender justice is a state where fair treatment is created for men and women by considering experiences, needs, difficulties, concerns as women and also as men Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and defense and security activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.

Gender mainstreaming (PUG) is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs.

Article 6

Protection of women from violence includes protection of women in the household, in the community, in the workplace and in conflict and disaster areas.

Protection of women from violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes women with disabilities, elderly women.

CHAPTER XII

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 33

Every person who deliberately does not provide protection to women resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

If an official appointed to administer protection does not carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the applicable laws and regulations.

Service managers who carry out service duties that violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms of the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 21

The regional government is obliged to supervise the implementation of protection for women from acts of violence.

Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out with professional, transparent and accountable principles.

Article 13

Women victims of violence in the family environment, community including in conflict areas and in the workplace have the right to be empowered.

Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed to create conditions that allow women's potential to develop, work and earn a living independently and not depend on others.

Article 19

Handling as referred to in Article 9 is carried out in an integrated manner by related SKPD and/or service institutions that handle the protection of women from acts of violence.

The provision of integrated services is coordinated by BPPKB or another name which will be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

The provision of integrated services is in accordance with applicable legislation.

Article 11

The provision of integrated services for women victims of violence is carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, with empathy, non-discrimination, easily accessible, and with guaranteed confidentiality.

CHAPTER VI

ASSISTANCE

Article 16

Assistance is carried out by persons or institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of women victims of violence and have cooperated with integrated service providers.

CHAPTER XI

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 30

Every woman victim of acts of violence has the right to obtain integrated protection, information, and services.

SUPPLEMENT TO THE REGIONAL GAZETTE OF PASER REGENCY NUMBER 45

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASER REGENCY

NUMBER 6 OF 2016

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASER REGENCY

NUMBER 6 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

Article 31

Identification of victims is the collection of data on women who are victims of violence. Data collection is carried out by SKPD and/or service institutions established by the regional government that are authorized to carry out that function.

Legal aid is legal services to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.

Medical rehabilitation is medical services, in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

Psychosocial rehabilitation is a service provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide social support so that victims have a sense of confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems Social reintegration is an effort by the regional government through SKPD and/or service institutions together with the community to assist women victims of violence in adapting and integrating in the community environment where they live.

Repatriation assistance is an effort by the regional government through SKPD and/or service institutions to assist in returning women victims of violence to their homes or other intended places safely.

Empowerment is the regional government through SKPD and/or service institutions providing assistance to women victims of violence in the form of training and opening access to capital with the aim that women victims of violence can be independent.

Article 22

The community can supervise the implementation of protection for women from acts of violence organized by the regional government with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Regent or DPRD.

Article 15

The Manpower Office and the Cooperatives and Small and Medium Enterprises Office in conducting entrepreneurship training as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (3) letter a in the form of: strengthening independence, namely increasing knowledge, skills and work skills of women victims of violence to more easily obtain employment;

productive economic enterprises, namely fostering the entrepreneurial spirit and skills of women victims of violence in the economic field who are not accommodated to work in the formal sector.

Productive economic enterprises as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b include forms of business that can be carried out by women.

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

Article 21

The regional government is obliged to supervise the implementation of protection for women from acts of violence.

Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out with professional, transparent and accountable principles.

Article 31

Identification of victims is the collection of data on women who are victims of violence. Data collection is carried out by SKPD and/or service institutions established by the regional government that are authorized to carry out that function.

Legal aid is legal services to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.

Medical rehabilitation is medical services, in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

Psychosocial rehabilitation is a service provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide social support so that victims have a sense of confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems Social reintegration is an effort by the regional government through SKPD and/or service institutions together with the community to assist women victims of violence in adapting and integrating in the community environment where they live.

Repatriation assistance is an effort by the regional government through SKPD and/or service institutions to assist in returning women victims of violence to their homes or other intended places safely.

Empowerment is the regional government through SKPD and/or service institutions providing assistance to women victims of violence in the form of training and opening access to capital with the aim that women victims of violence can be independent.

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

CHAPTER XI

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 30

Every woman victim of acts of violence has the right to obtain integrated protection, information, and services.

The Manpower Office and the Cooperatives and Small and Medium Enterprises Office empower women victims of violence.

developing models for increasing women's economic productivity through partnerships between regional government and the community.

productive economic enterprises, namely fostering the entrepreneurial spirit and skills of women victims of violence in the economic field who are not accommodated to work in the formal sector.

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

productive economic enterprises, namely fostering the entrepreneurial spirit and skills of women victims of violence in the economic field who are not accommodated to work in the formal sector.

Productive economic enterprises as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b include forms of business that can be carried out by women.

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

Article 2

Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women;

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

The best interests of victims means that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASER REGENCY

NUMBER 6 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region of Paser Regency.

Regent is the Regent of Paser Women are all women who are both inside and outside the household Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.

Physical violence is an act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Household neglect is any person who neglects another person in their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party given at the stage of investigation, inquiry, determination and upon examination in court hearings.

Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.

Service is an action that must be immediately taken to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim (woman) will, is or has occurred.

Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.

Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children.

Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house Gender is a characteristic inherent to men and women that is socially and culturally constructed.

Gender injustice is a system and structure in which both men and women become victims of that system.

Gender justice is a state where fair treatment is created for men and women by considering experiences, needs, difficulties, concerns as women and also as men Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and defense and security activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.

Gender mainstreaming (PUG) is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs.

productive economic enterprises, namely fostering the entrepreneurial spirit and skills of women victims of violence in the economic field who are not accommodated to work in the formal sector.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

Article 2

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women;

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

The best interests of victims means that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Handling

Article 19

Handling as referred to in Article 9 is carried out in an integrated manner by related SKPD and/or service institutions that handle the protection of women from acts of violence.

ASSISTANCE

Article 22

The community can supervise the implementation of protection for women from acts of violence organized by the regional government with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Regent or DPRD.

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 33

Every person who deliberately does not provide protection to women resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Service managers who carry out service duties that violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms of the applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region of Paser Regency.

Regent is the Regent of Paser Women are all women who are both inside and outside the household Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.

Physical violence is an act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Household neglect is any person who neglects another person in their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party given at the stage of investigation, inquiry, determination and upon examination in court hearings.

Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.

Service is an action that must be immediately taken to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim (woman) will, is or has occurred.

Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.

Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children.

Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house Gender is a characteristic inherent to men and women that is socially and culturally constructed.

Gender injustice is a system and structure in which both men and women become victims of that system.

Gender justice is a state where fair treatment is created for men and women by considering experiences, needs, difficulties, concerns as women and also as men Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and defense and security activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.

Gender mainstreaming (PUG) is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs.

Article 31

Identification of victims is the collection of data on women who are victims of violence. Data collection is carried out by SKPD and/or service institutions established by the regional government that are authorized to carry out that function.

Legal aid is legal services to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.

Medical rehabilitation is medical services, in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

Psychosocial rehabilitation is a service provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide social support so that victims have a sense of confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems Social reintegration is an effort by the regional government through SKPD and/or service institutions together with the community to assist women victims of violence in adapting and integrating in the community environment where they live.

Repatriation assistance is an effort by the regional government through SKPD and/or service institutions to assist in returning women victims of violence to their homes or other intended places safely.

Empowerment is the regional government through SKPD and/or service institutions providing assistance to women victims of violence in the form of training and opening access to capital with the aim that women victims of violence can be independent.

Article 32

Every woman victim has the right to obtain assistance both psychologically and legally and to obtain guarantees of her rights relating to her status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 11

The provision of integrated services for women victims of violence is carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, with empathy, non-discrimination, easily accessible, and with guaranteed confidentiality.

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

SANCTION PROVISIONS

The provision of integrated services for women victims of violence is carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, with empathy, non-discrimination, easily accessible, and with guaranteed confidentiality.

Article 32

Every woman victim has the right to obtain assistance both psychologically and legally and to obtain guarantees of her rights relating to her status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

The community can supervise the implementation of protection for women from acts of violence organized by the regional government with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Regent or DPRD.

ASSISTANCE

Article 16

Assistance is carried out by persons or institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of women victims of violence and have cooperated with integrated service providers.

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

Household neglect is any person who neglects another person in their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party given at the stage of investigation, inquiry, determination and upon examination in court hearings.

Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.

Service is an action that must be immediately taken to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim (woman) will, is or has occurred.

Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.

Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children.

Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house Gender is a characteristic inherent to men and women that is socially and culturally constructed.

Gender injustice is a system and structure in which both men and women become victims of that system.

Gender justice is a state where fair treatment is created for men and women by considering experiences, needs, difficulties, concerns as women and also as men Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and defense and security activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.

Gender mainstreaming (PUG) is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASER REGENCY

NUMBER 6 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I.	GENERAL

To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against women, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Such a view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against women physically, psychologically, sexually, and neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate violence against women.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), therefore it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the 1945 Constitution fourth amendment, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

Regional governments also have the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against women. For this purpose regional governments need regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against women.

CHAPTER XII

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 33

Every person who deliberately does not provide protection to women resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

If an official appointed to administer protection does not carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the applicable laws and regulations.

Service managers who carry out service duties that violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms of the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 19

Handling as referred to in Article 9 is carried out in an integrated manner by related SKPD and/or service institutions that handle the protection of women from acts of violence.

The provision of integrated services is coordinated by BPPKB or another name which will be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

The provision of integrated services is in accordance with applicable legislation.

Article 14

The Manpower Office and the Cooperatives and Small and Medium Enterprises Office empower women victims of violence.

In empowering women as referred to in paragraph (1), it is implemented in accordance with the people's economic empowerment program.

The people's economic empowerment program as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out through: increasing the economic productivity of regional women by conducting entrepreneurship training for women in micro and small businesses;

developing models for increasing women's economic productivity through partnerships between regional government and the community.

Article 29

Neglect as referred to in Article 21 letter e, includes: Every person is prohibited from neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person.

Neglect as referred to in paragraph (1) also applies to every person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Article 2

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women;

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

The best interests of victims means that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.
